newsitem.title: UK: Pearson dives on Penguin accounting news.
newsitem.headline: Pearson dives on Penguin accounting news.

text.p: Shares in Pearson Plc dived on Thursday, shedding as much as 7.7 percent at one point, after the media group said it had uncovered improper accounting at its Penguin USA books unit.
The company said that it may have to make up a charge against 1996 profits of as much as 100 million stg.
At 0837 GMT, the shares were down 27p to 736-1/2, well above the day's low of 690 set earlier during pre-market trading.

"Until it's clear what the impact on cash flow will be, it's hard to make sense of it," said one analyst. "The one thing that is clear is that there's a lot of room for improvement in (Pearson's) units."

The company said that the accounting problems at its trade book publishing subsidiary in the U.S. date back to 1991 and relate to unauthorised discounts given to customers in return for early payments.
